description: "Cifre antiche": cifrari of Cardinals Antonio and Francesco Barberini and of the generals of the Church Carlo and Taddeo Barberini (OPAC).
use: Keys for the Barberini secretariat and family correspondence: Barb. lat. 9892 (Revelo 1641), the Mancini/Ricci/Millanta Madrid series, nunciature traffic 1623-1644.

description: "Cifre antiche": cifrari of Cardinals Francesco, Antonio and Carlo Barberini (OPAC).
use: As Barb. lat. 9914; Carlo Barberini (cardinal 1653) brings it into the 1650s-1670s.

description: Cifrario enclosed in Domenico Giannuzzi's letters to Marco Gallio, nuncio at Cologne (OPAC: "a f. 141r, è accluso il cifrario").
use: Key for the cipher passages of the same 38 letters (candidates.json row) and possibly Gallio's Cologne nunciature 1659-1666.

date: saec. XVIII per the catalogue (an anagram slip on f. 105 names Pietro Mocenigo and Clement X, i.e. 1670-1676)
description: "Anonymi Cryptographicae scripturae epitome per numeros et vocabula digesta", 144 ff., Latin vocabulary to number groups (inc. "as in ate 15, adde tenet 250", des. "1071 Purpuratus"); Colonna library stamp (Vattasso-Carusi, Codices Vaticani latini 9852-10300, 1914).
seen: f. 1r and f. 105r opened (105r is an anagram slip, not cipher); manifest https://digi.vatlib.it/iiif/MSS_Vat.lat.9955/manifest.json
use: A Latin numeric code of the later 17th c.; test against undeciphered Roman/Venetian numeric codes of 1660-1700.

shelfmark: BAV, Urb. lat. 948 (and its copy Urb. lat. 949)
date: sec. XV (948), sec. XVI (949, a copy)
description: "Scriptura occulta, vulgo cifra, Friderici II, Urbini ducis", 101 ff. (inc. "A B L A A l g r f"). f. 50r, opened, is a full polyalphabetic table: alphabet rows M-L, each a shifted mixed alphabet, headed "+ A T G +". Not the same book as Urb. lat. 998 (Federico's cifrario 1440-1469, DECODE R1413-R1468, already in the repo).
use: Federico da Montefeltro's table cipher; check the claimed 15th-c. date and look for Urbino letters enciphered with it. Not in the repo ledgers (only named in research/sweep_2026-11_vatican_rome/README.md).

description: Cifrario used by the Jesuit missionaries in China (OPAC item 214436).
use: Key for Jesuit China mission ciphers (Propaganda / ARSI correspondence).

description: "Tractatus de cifris", Latin, inc. "Hi qui maximis rebus agendis praesunt, in dies experiuntur"; the prologue promises a way "ad aliorum occulta indaganda" (cryptanalysis) as well as to hide one's own.
use: A 15th-c. cipher-breaking treatise: reference for Quattrocento practice, possibly with worked examples. Not in the repo.

description: Claudio Tolomei, "Introduzione alle cifre volgari" (inc. "Gli antichi egittii usavano le lettere ieroglife").
